name: Aurelius House Silk Banded-Collar
description:
Aurelius House is one of three surviving Spire-tier couture labels operating out of GLMZ, and their Silk Banded-Collar shirt is as close to a casual offering as they make — which means it still costs more than most people's monthly rent. The fabric is cultured mulberry silk, grown in a controlled bioreactor environment and processed without mechanical intervention, resulting in a cloth of extraordinary consistency and sheen. The cut is a relaxed, long-body silhouette with a mandarin collar, mother-of-pearl buttons sourced from a Pacific coastal cooperative, and French seams throughout.

The shirt is unbranded externally — not even an interior tag, just a small hand-stitched thread mark in a color specific to the season's production run, which Aurelius clients know how to read. It comes in a range of colors chosen seasonally: this cycle includes deep burgundy, a grey-green called 'Moss Water,' and a warm ivory. The Spire clients who wear this are not trying to signal wealth — they're past that. This is the shirt you wear when signaling anything would feel beneath you.
what_it_says: You are so far past needing to prove anything that you've come all the way back around to wearing a plain shirt. The people who matter know what this is. Everyone else doesn't need to.
worn_by: people for whom anonymity is a luxury
story_hooks: Aurelius House's head designer has started quietly accepting commissions from clients outside the Spire — a breach of the label's founding charter — and the other founding partners are considering a legal action that could tear the house apart.

The hand-stitched thread mark system used by Aurelius to authenticate garments has been decoded by a the Gray Zone counterfeiter producing near-perfect replicas, and Aurelius is trying to find them without involving law enforcement (which would require public disclosure of the authentication system).

A character finds themselves in possession of an Aurelius Banded-Collar with a thread mark from a production run that was never officially released — meaning either it's a very sophisticated fake, or it came from somewhere inside Aurelius that isn't supposed to exist.

physical_description.visual_profile: An understated elegance that reads as effortless wealth. The mandarin collar sits close to the neck without constraining, while the long-body silhouette drapes with fluid grace. On a person, it projects quiet confidence—the kind of garment that doesn't announce itself but commands attention through pure refinement. The overall impression is almost meditative: expensive restraint.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed yet intentional. Not oversized, but generously cut through the shoulders and torso, allowing the silk to move with the body rather than cling. The long body extends past typical shirt length, creating an elongated silhouette that suggests both comfort and deliberate proportion.
physical_description.primary_material: Cultured mulberry silk, grown in bioreactor and hand-processed. The consistency is flawless, with a subtle natural sheen that catches light without gloss.
physical_description.texture: Impossibly smooth to the eye, with a soft luster that suggests touch without demanding it. The weave is so fine and regular it appears almost liquid when photographed. French seams create imperceptible internal structure.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep burgundy, grey-green (Moss Water), or warm ivory depending on seasonal run. Each color is muted and sophisticated—no vibrance, only depth.
physical_description.closures: Mother-of-pearl buttons sourced from Pacific coastal cooperative. Buttons are small, subtle, and perfectly spaced down the front placket.
distinctive_features: French seams throughout—visible only to those who know what to look for
Long-body cut extending beyond standard shirt length
Interior hand-stitched thread mark in seasonal color—readable only to Aurelius clientele as production run identifier
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1 luxury—beyond luxury. This is Spire-tier couture. The price point exceeds monthly rent for most GLMZ residents.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Aurelius House clientele who exist in the rarefied upper echelons of GLMZ society. Signaling anything would be beneath them; this garment is for those whose wealth is so established it needs no announcement. The wearer is likely a corpo executive, board member, or legacy money. To wear this is to participate in a conversation only Spire dwellers understand.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new. With wear, it softens further, becoming even more beautiful. The silk develops a subtle patina of use that only enhances its value. Aurelius clients have these for decades.
